questions.q: A young man on his way to catch a train for a job interview would not let his friend chase boys who had thrown stones. What does the article draw from this?
options: One who is serious about a goal has no time for distractions – and the believer’s goal is the Hereafter
Yes. Patience keeps the journey on course.
Travel plans matter more than friendship
Not quite. The article says: One who is serious about a goal has no time for distractions – and the believer’s goal is the Hereafter.
Young people should avoid quarrels in public
Not quite. The article says: One who is serious about a goal has no time for distractions – and the believer’s goal is the Hereafter.
Children should never be punished
Not quite. The article says: One who is serious about a goal has no time for distractions – and the believer’s goal is the Hereafter.
questions.rationale: “One who is serious about the Hereafter does not want to get involved at all, in issues that will divert him from his goal.”

questions.q: Maurice Wilson wrote in his diary that he would reach the summit of Everest on his birthday, and died on the mountain. Why does the article tell his story?
options: To praise the courage of explorers
Not quite. The article says: To show how people feel sure of “tomorrow” while moving, unaware, towards death.
To warn against mountaineering
Not quite. The article says: To show how people feel sure of “tomorrow” while moving, unaware, towards death.
To show how people feel sure of “tomorrow” while moving, unaware, towards death
Well read. “Life is absolutely uncertain, yet people imagine it to be absolutely certain.”
To show that planning always fails
Not quite. The article says: To show how people feel sure of “tomorrow” while moving, unaware, towards death.
questions.rationale: “Everyone thinks that he is advancing towards the peak of success… In actual fact, everyone is heading towards a destination where there will be no one to welcome him other than Death.”

questions.q: According to the article, how does the Quran describe the relation between men and women?
options: As identical in every function
Not quite. The article says: As a pair that complete each other – equal in respect, different in roles.
As rivals for the same roles
Not quite. The article says: As a pair that complete each other – equal in respect, different in roles.
As a pair that complete each other – equal in respect, different in roles
Correct. Nature works on complementarity.
As independent of each other
Not quite. The article says: As a pair that complete each other – equal in respect, different in roles.
questions.rationale: “Nature functions on the principle of complementarity… ‘Men and women are equal in respect and different in roles’.”

questions.q: What, says the article, most easily pulls the mind away during prayer – and what guards against it?
options: Negative thinking; it is guarded against by patience
Yes. That is why patience is mentioned together with prayer.
Tiredness; guarded against by sleep
Not quite. The article says: Negative thinking; it is guarded against by patience.
Hunger; guarded against by eating first
Not quite. The article says: Negative thinking; it is guarded against by patience.
Noise; guarded against by solitude
Not quite. The article says: Negative thinking; it is guarded against by patience.
questions.rationale: “The most powerful thing that can shift one’s focus away from something is negative thinking… Offering prayer with humility and utter sincerity is possible only for the person who before prayer has developed positive thinking.”

questions.q: On seeing an unfamiliar African tree, what thought came to the author?
options: That nature grows without any design
Not quite. The article says: That it is as if “Made by God” were written on everything, so that God may be recognised through His creation.
That trees ought to be labelled with their names
Not quite. The article says: That it is as if “Made by God” were written on everything, so that God may be recognised through His creation.
That African trees are finer than others
Not quite. The article says: That it is as if “Made by God” were written on everything, so that God may be recognised through His creation.
That it is as if “Made by God” were written on everything, so that God may be recognised through His creation
Right. The craftsmanship itself announces the Maker.
questions.rationale: “It is as if God wrote the words ‘Made by God’ on everything and then kept Himself hidden from people’s vision so that they could recognize Him from the things that He has created.”

questions.q: Why, according to the article, does the Quran tell of many earlier prophets and not only of the Prophet Muhammad?
options: To show which prophet was the greatest
Not quite. The article says: So that believers may find guidance in how each prophet dealt with his situation.
To record the history of ancient kings
Not quite. The article says: So that believers may find guidance in how each prophet dealt with his situation.
So that believers may find guidance in how each prophet dealt with his situation
Yes. “These are whom God guided aright, so follow their guidance.”
To correct the dates given by historians
Not quite. The article says: So that believers may find guidance in how each prophet dealt with his situation.
questions.rationale: “It was so that the Prophet of Islam and his ummah might learn valuable lessons from the ways in which these prophets dealt with the situations in which they found themselves.”

questions.q: The article places Jesus’ words “Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you” beside a verse of the Quran. Which one?
options: “Every soul shall taste death”
Not quite. The article says: “Repel evil with good and he who is your enemy will become your dearest friend”.
“Repel evil with good and he who is your enemy will become your dearest friend”
Exactly (41:34). The same teaching is found in both.
“For you your religion; for me mine”
Not quite. The article says: “Repel evil with good and he who is your enemy will become your dearest friend”.
“There is no compulsion in religion”
Not quite. The article says: “Repel evil with good and he who is your enemy will become your dearest friend”.
questions.rationale: “The same teaching is echoed in the Quran: And good deeds and evil deeds are not alike. Repel evil with good and he who is your enemy will become your dearest friend.”

questions.q: “We alternate these days among mankind,” says the Quran. How should a person respond to gaining or losing power, in the article’s view?
options: By protesting until power is restored
Not quite. The article says: Without pride when in power and without bitterness when out of it, for both are tests.
By avoiding public life altogether
Not quite. The article says: Without pride when in power and without bitterness when out of it, for both are tests.
By holding on to power at any cost
Not quite. The article says: Without pride when in power and without bitterness when out of it, for both are tests.
Without pride when in power and without bitterness when out of it, for both are tests
Yes. Attention should stay on one’s own responsibilities.
questions.rationale: “When he is granted power, he should not suffer from pride and arrogance. And when man finds himself in a state of subjugation, he should not fall prey to negative psychology.”

questions.q: What does “tightrope walking” mean in what the article calls the dictionary of wisdom?
options: Avoiding every decision
Not quite. The article says: Keeping a wise balance between one’s desires and outer realities.
Taking risks to entertain others
Not quite. The article says: Keeping a wise balance between one’s desires and outer realities.
Living without any desires
Not quite. The article says: Keeping a wise balance between one’s desires and outer realities.
Keeping a wise balance between one’s desires and outer realities
Right. Leaning to either side brings a fall.
questions.rationale: “You have to maintain a wise balance between your personal desires and external realities. This is the real art of life.”

questions.q: At a book fair the author saw a dog searching for food, unaware of the books around it. What did the sight suggest to him?
options: That animals should be kept out of public places
Not quite. The article says: That most people move among God’s signs without noticing them or asking life’s great questions.
That most people move among God’s signs without noticing them or asking life’s great questions
Well read. People are “lost in the creation, and not in the Creator.”
That books are of little use to the hungry
Not quite. The article says: That most people move among God’s signs without noticing them or asking life’s great questions.
That knowledge belongs only to scholars
Not quite. The article says: That most people move among God’s signs without noticing them or asking life’s great questions.
questions.rationale: “God’s signs… are visible everywhere, but most of us human beings move around in blind ignorance of them.”
